prophet-muhammad.name: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
prophet-muhammad.fullName: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib al-Qurashi
prophet-muhammad.arabicFullName: محمد بن عبد الله بن عبد المطلب القرشي الهاشمي ﷺ
prophet-muhammad.grade: Final Messenger of Allah & Seal of the Prophets
prophet-muhammad.ibnHajarGrade: Sayyid al-Awwaleen wal-Akhireen (Master of the First and the Last)
prophet-muhammad.dhahabiGrade: The Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds
prophet-muhammad.biography: The final messenger and prophet sent by Allah to humanity, recipient of the Holy Qur'an, and embodiment of divine wisdom and exemplary prophetic character. Every authentic hadith traces back either directly to his sacred speech (qawl), noble actions (fi'l), tacit approvals (taqrir), or physical and moral description (sifah).
prophet-muhammad.scholarlyContribution: The primary source of the Sunnah, the second foundational source of Islamic law, ethics, creed, and spiritual life.
students: The Sahabah (Companions) - may Allah be pleased with all of them

al-bukhari.name: Imam al-Bukhari
al-bukhari.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Ju'fi al-Bukhari
al-bukhari.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله محمد بن إسماعيل بن إبراهيم بن المغيرة الجعفي البخاري
al-bukhari.grade: Amir al-Mu'minin fil-Hadith (Commander of the Faithful in Hadith)
al-bukhari.ibnHajarGrade: Mountain of memorization, master of hadith criticism and defect analysis
al-bukhari.dhahabiGrade: The unequaled master of all Hadith masters, compiler of the most authentic book after the Qur'an
al-bukhari.biography: Born in Bukhara in 194 AH, Imam al-Bukhari was orphaned in childhood and blessed with miraculous memory. He traveled across the entire Islamic realm for over sixteen years, examining over 600,000 traditions to compile "Al-Jami' al-Sahih", the most rigorously authenticated collection in history. Before recording every single hadith in his Sahih, he performed ritual purification and prayed two units of istikharah prayer.
al-bukhari.scholarlyContribution: Established the highest criteria for hadith authenticity (requiring positive proof of direct contemporary meeting and unblemished moral integrity). Author of Sahih al-Bukhari, Al-Tarikh al-Kabir, and Al-Adab al-Mufrad.

umar-ibn-al-khattab.name: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab
umar-ibn-al-khattab.fullName: Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Qurashi al-Adawi
umar-ibn-al-khattab.arabicFullName: أبو حفص عمر بن الخطاب بن نفيل القرشي العدوي رضي الله عنه
umar-ibn-al-khattab.ibnHajarGrade: Second Rightly-Guided Caliph, distinguished between truth and falsehood (Al-Faruq)
umar-ibn-al-khattab.dhahabiGrade: One of the ten promised Paradise, supreme in justice and governance
umar-ibn-al-khattab.biography: Known as Al-Faruq (the one who distinguishes between truth and falsehood), 'Umar was the second Rightly-Guided Caliph. Renowned for his uncompromising justice, deep legal understanding, and humility. The Prophet ﷺ said of him: "If there were to be a prophet after me, it would be 'Umar." He narrated foundational traditions of Islam, including the world-renowned Hadith of Intentions and the Hadith of Jibril.
umar-ibn-al-khattab.scholarlyContribution: Narrated over 500 hadiths; instituted the Islamic Hijri calendar, the compilation of the Qur'an council, and systematic public records.

aisha-bint-abi-bakr.name: 'A'isha bint Abi Bakr
aisha-bint-abi-bakr.arabicFullName: أم المؤمنين عائشة بنت أبي بكر الصديق القرشية التيمية رضي الله عنها
aisha-bint-abi-bakr.grade: Mother of the Believers & Foremost Jurist of the Sahabah
aisha-bint-abi-bakr.ibnHajarGrade: Faqihat al-Ummah (Jurist of the Nation), the most knowledgeable woman in history
aisha-bint-abi-bakr.dhahabiGrade: The beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, profound in Quranic interpretation, medicine, and poetry
aisha-bint-abi-bakr.biography: Wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and daughter of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. She possessed an extraordinary intellect and exceptional memory, preserving the intimate prophetic traditions, daily ethics, prayer rituals, and household sunnah that no one else could observe. Sahabah regularly consulted her on intricate legal and inheritance dilemmas.
aisha-bint-abi-bakr.scholarlyContribution: Narrated 2,210 hadiths, ranking among the top four most prolific narrators. Renowned for her rigorous critical analysis (istidrak) of reports.

abu-hurairah.name: Abu Hurairah
abu-hurairah.arabicFullName: عبد الرحمن بن صخر الدوسي رضي الله عنه
abu-hurairah.grade: Sahabi 'Adl - Most Prolific Narrator of Hadith
abu-hurairah.ibnHajarGrade: The foremost memorizer among the Companions, certified by prophetic du'a for unfailing memory
abu-hurairah.dhahabiGrade: Imam al-Hafiz, the vessel of prophetic sunnah
abu-hurairah.biography: Embraced Islam in 7 AH during the conquest of Khaybar and dedicated himself entirely to the companionship of the Prophet ﷺ as a prominent resident of Ahl al-Suffah. The Prophet ﷺ made a special supplication that Abu Hurairah would never forget what he heard. He devoted the remainder of his life to teaching and transmitting hadiths to hundreds of students.
abu-hurairah.scholarlyContribution: Narrated 5,374 hadiths, the highest number of any Companion. Over 800 scholars and successors transmitted hadiths on his authority.

anas-ibn-malik.name: Anas ibn Malik
anas-ibn-malik.fullName: Anas ibn Malik ibn al-Nadr al-Ansari al-Khazraji
anas-ibn-malik.arabicFullName: أبو حمزة أنس بن مالك بن النضر الأنصاري الخزرجي رضي الله عنه
anas-ibn-malik.grade: Sahabi 'Adl - Personal Servant of the Prophet ﷺ
anas-ibn-malik.ibnHajarGrade: Served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years; blessed with longevity, knowledge, and righteous progeny
anas-ibn-malik.dhahabiGrade: Mufti, Qari, and last surviving Companion in Basra
anas-ibn-malik.biography: Presented by his mother Umm Sulaym to serve the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at the age of ten upon the Hijrah to Madinah. He served the Prophet ﷺ continuously for ten years with deep loyalty and observed the Prophet's most intimate manners and kindness. The Prophet ﷺ prayed for him: "O Allah, grant him abundance in wealth and children, and bless him in all You bestow upon him."
anas-ibn-malik.scholarlyContribution: Narrated 2,286 hadiths. Transmitted crucial insights on prophetic temperament, humility, prayer conduct, and daily etiquette.

abdullah-ibn-umar.name: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar
abdullah-ibn-umar.fullName: Abu Abd al-Rahman Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab al-Qurashi
abdullah-ibn-umar.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الرحمن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب القرشي العدوي رضي الله عنهما
abdullah-ibn-umar.grade: Sahabi 'Adl - Exemplar of Strict Adherence to the Sunnah
abdullah-ibn-umar.ibnHajarGrade: Eminent jurist, scrupulous worshiper, famed for matching the Prophet's footsteps in every detail
abdullah-ibn-umar.dhahabiGrade: Imam, master of Madinan jurisprudence, uncompromising in avoiding political strife
abdullah-ibn-umar.biography: Son of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Known throughout Islamic history for his passionate, exact replication of prophetic behavior—even sitting where the Prophet sat and walking along the same paths. He was revered for his intense piety, generous charity, and resolute refusal of judicial or caliphal offices during periods of civil conflict.
abdullah-ibn-umar.scholarlyContribution: Narrated 2,630 hadiths. His narrations through his freed slave Nafi' and Imam Malik form the renowned "Golden Chain" (Silsilat al-Dhahab).
students: Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar

al-humaydi.name: Al-Humaydi
al-humaydi.fullName: Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr ibn Isa al-Qurashi al-Asadi al-Humaydi
al-humaydi.arabicFullName: أبو بكر عبد الله بن الزبير بن عيسى القرشي الأسدي الحميدي
al-humaydi.grade: Thiqah Hafiz Faqih (Trustworthy, Master Memorizer, Jurist)
al-humaydi.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Hafiz Faqih, foremost companion and transmitter of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah
al-humaydi.dhahabiGrade: Imam, Mufti of the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah, author of the renowned Musnad
al-humaydi.biography: The leading master of Hadith in Makkah and close companion of Imam al-Shafi'i. Imam al-Bukhari chose to open his Sahih with a narration from al-Humaydi (Hadith #1 on Intentions) as an auspicious blessing and homage to his venerable Makkan teacher. Known for his steadfast adherence to Sunnah and defense of orthodox creed.
al-humaydi.scholarlyContribution: Author of Musnad al-Humaydi; transmitted the vast Makkan heritage of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah with exquisite accuracy.

sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.name: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.fullName: Abu Muhammad Sufyan ibn Uyaynah ibn Abi Imran al-Hilali al-Kufi thumma al-Makki
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.arabicFullName: أبو محمد سفيان بن عيينة بن ميمون الهلالي الكوفي ثم المكي
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.grade: Thiqah Thabt Imam Hujjah (Trustworthy, Firm, Master Authority)
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt Hafiz, leading scholar of the Hijaz alongside Malik
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.dhahabiGrade: Shaikh al-Islam, one of the foundational pillars of Islamic scholarship
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.biography: Born in Kufa in 107 AH and settled in Makkah. He attended lessons of the great Tabi'in at an astonishingly early age and met eighty Successors. Imam al-Shafi'i said: "Were it not for Malik and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, the knowledge of the Hijaz would have perished." He served as the primary hadith authority in the Holy Mosque of Makkah for over fifty years.
sufyan-ibn-uyaynah.scholarlyContribution: Transmitted thousands of traditions with supreme precision, linking Kufan and Hijazi hadith traditions.

yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.name: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari
yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.fullName: Abu Sa'id Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Qays ibn Amr al-Ansari al-Najjari al-Madani
yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.arabicFullName: أبو سعيد يحيى بن سعيد بن قيس بن عمرو الأنصاري النجاري المدني
yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, distinguished judge of Madinah and subsequently Iraq
yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.dhahabiGrade: Imam, Hujjah, and one of the pivotal transmitters around whom hadiths revolve
yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.biography: An illustrious Ansar jurist and grandson of a Companion who fought at Badr. He served as the Chief Judge (Qadi) of Madinah during the Umayyad era. Renowned for his vast knowledge, judicial precision, and meticulous verification of texts. He is the central pivot through whom the hadith of intentions ("Actions are judged by motives") reached hundreds of scholars.
yahya-ibn-said-al-ansari.scholarlyContribution: Central link in the transmission of Madinan sunnah and pivotal narrator for the school of Imam Malik.

muhammad-ibn-ibrahim.name: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi
muhammad-ibn-ibrahim.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith ibn Khalid al-Taymi al-Qurashi
muhammad-ibn-ibrahim.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله محمد بن إبراهيم بن الحارث بن خالد التيمي القرشي المدني
muhammad-ibn-ibrahim.dhahabiGrade: Eminent successor, scholar of Madinah, precise narrator
muhammad-ibn-ibrahim.biography: A notable Successor belonging to Banu Taym in Madinah. His father Ibrahim was among the early emigrants. He acquired deep legal erudition from senior Companions and early Successors, and is recognized for his singular fidelity in narrating the hadith of Intentions directly from Alqama ibn Waqqas.
muhammad-ibn-ibrahim.scholarlyContribution: Crucial sole transmitter connecting Alqama ibn Waqqas to Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari in the foundational hadith of Islam.

alqama-ibn-waqqas.name: Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi
alqama-ibn-waqqas.fullName: Alqama ibn Waqqas ibn Muhsin ibn Kalada al-Laythi al-Madani
alqama-ibn-waqqas.arabicFullName: علقمة بن وقاص بن محصن بن كلدة الليثي المدني
alqama-ibn-waqqas.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, senior Successor who witnessed the Khulafa al-Rashidin
alqama-ibn-waqqas.dhahabiGrade: One of the prominent early scholars of Madinah
alqama-ibn-waqqas.biography: A venerable Senior Successor who lived in Madinah during the golden era of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs. He was present in the Prophet's Mosque during the caliphate of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and personally stood beneath the minbar when 'Umar delivered his momentous sermon stating: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Actions are but by intentions..."
alqama-ibn-waqqas.scholarlyContribution: The sole link who received and preserved 'Umar ibn al-Khattab's narration of the intention hadith for succeeding generations.

malik-ibn-anas.name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
malik-ibn-anas.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi al-Madani
malik-ibn-anas.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله مالك بن أنس بن مالك بن أبي عامر الأصبحي الحميري المدني
malik-ibn-anas.grade: Imam Dar al-Hijrah (Leader of the Abode of Migration)
malik-ibn-anas.ibnHajarGrade: Head of the scholars of Madinah, model of piety, author of Al-Muwatta
malik-ibn-anas.dhahabiGrade: Shaikh al-Islam, Master of jurists, the undisputed sun of scholars
malik-ibn-anas.biography: Founder of the Maliki school of Islamic jurisprudence and author of Al-Muwatta', the earliest surviving codification of Islamic law and hadith. Malik was so revered in Madinah that he would never mount an animal in the city out of reverence for the earth that embraced the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When narrating hadith, he bathed, applied perfume, and wore his finest garment.
malik-ibn-anas.scholarlyContribution: Compiler of Al-Muwatta'; formulator of the principle of the 'Amal (living practice) of Ahl al-Madinah.

ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.name: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.fullName: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri al-Qurashi
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.arabicFullName: أبو بكر محمد بن مسلم بن عبيد الله بن شهاب الزهري القرشي المدني
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.grade: Imam al-Hafiz - Master of Sunnah and Hadith Preservation
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.ibnHajarGrade: Faqih, Hafiz, universally acclaimed for encyclopedic retention; pioneer in official hadith codification
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.dhahabiGrade: The great ocean of knowledge, central axis of the prophetic sunnah
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.biography: Commissioned by the righteous Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz to lead the first formal state compilation of the Prophetic Hadith. He studied under the Seven Jurists of Madinah and retained narrations with legendary fidelity. Umar II declared: "Adhere to Ibn Shihab, for you will not find anyone more knowledgeable in the past sunnah than him."
ibn-shihab-al-zuhri.scholarlyContribution: Pioneered systematic written recordation of hadith and transmission chains (isnad), preserving tens of thousands of narrations.

urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.name: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Urwah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam al-Qurashi al-Asadi
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله عروة بن الزبير بن العوام القرشي الأسدي المدني
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.grade: One of the Seven Great Jurists of Madinah (Al-Fuqaha' al-Sab'ah)
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, ocean of knowledge, foremost transmitter of his maternal aunt Aisha
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.dhahabiGrade: Imam, leader of the Successors, legendary for his patience and continuous prayer
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.biography: Son of the illustrious Companion Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Asma' bint Abi Bakr, and nephew of Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha. He spent years in 'A'isha's home learning her hadiths, jurisprudence, and historical accounts directly. Renowned for his extraordinary endurance during an amputation, refusing wine for anesthesia and dedicating his mind to prayer.
urwah-ibn-al-zubayr.scholarlyContribution: Authored the earliest written accounts of the Prophetic Biography (Maghazi / Sirah) and transmitted a substantial portion of 'A'isha's legal corpus.

said-ibn-al-musayyib.name: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib
said-ibn-al-musayyib.fullName: Abu Muhammad Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib ibn Hazn al-Qurashi al-Makhzumi
said-ibn-al-musayyib.arabicFullName: أبو محمد سعيد بن المسيب بن حزن القرشي المخزومي المدني
said-ibn-al-musayyib.ibnHajarGrade: Foremost scholar of Madinah, unanimously praised for knowledge, scrupulousness, and courage
said-ibn-al-musayyib.dhahabiGrade: The master of the Successors in knowledge and virtue without dispute
said-ibn-al-musayyib.biography: Universally hailed as "Sayyid al-Tabi'in" (The Master of the Successors). He married the daughter of Abu Hurairah to benefit from his knowledge and spent over fifty years attending the congregational prayers in the first row of the Prophet's Mosque. He was famed for his steadfast courage in the face of political tyranny.
said-ibn-al-musayyib.scholarlyContribution: The leading authority on the legal judgments and precedents of Umar ibn al-Khattab and senior Companions.

nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.name: Nafi' Mawla Ibn 'Umar
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Nafi' al-Madani Mawla Abd Allah ibn Umar
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله نافع المدني مولى عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.grade: Thiqah Thabt (Cornerstone of the Golden Chain)
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, pillar of Madinan hadith transmission
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.dhahabiGrade: The great jurist and memorizer, undisputed pillar in the Golden Chain
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.biography: The faithful freedman of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar who accompanied him for thirty years at home and on journeys, memorizing his statements and legal rulings. Imam al-Bukhari famously declared that the most authentic chain of narration on earth is: "Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar" (The Golden Chain).
nafi-mawla-ibn-umar.scholarlyContribution: Transmitted Ibn Umar's vast legal legacy and prophetic reports with unblemished accuracy.

shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.name: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.fullName: Abu Bisht Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj ibn al-Ward al-Ataki al-Basri
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.arabicFullName: أبو بسطام شعبة بن الحجاج العتكي الأزدي مولاهم الواسطي ثم البصري
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.grade: Amir al-Mu'minin fil-Hadith (Prince of Hadith in Iraq)
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Hafiz Mutqin, pioneer of narrator criticism (Al-Jarh wal-Ta'dil)
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.dhahabiGrade: The master of Hadith critics and the benchmark of precision in Basra
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.biography: Hailed by Sufyan al-Thawri as the "Commander of the Faithful in Hadith." Shu'bah was the very first scholar in Iraq to critically examine narrators' reliability and memory, inaugurating the crucial Islamic science of Al-Jarh wal-Ta'dil. He was famed for traveling hundreds of miles across deserts merely to verify a single preposition or word.
shuba-ibn-al-hajjaj.scholarlyContribution: Founded the rigorous scientific discipline of biographical narrator appraisal and chain verification.

sufyan-al-thawri.name: Sufyan al-Thawri
sufyan-al-thawri.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Thawri al-Kufi
sufyan-al-thawri.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله سفيان بن سعيد بن مسروق الثوري الكوفي
sufyan-al-thawri.ibnHajarGrade: Faqih, Hafiz, ascetic, universally regarded as a proof of God on earth in knowledge
sufyan-al-thawri.dhahabiGrade: Shaikh al-Islam, master of scholars in his era
sufyan-al-thawri.biography: One of the greatest scholars in Islamic history, revered for his immense knowledge of Hadith and Fiqh alongside profound asceticism (zuhd). When pressured by the Abbasid caliphate to accept the post of Chief Judge, he fled into exile rather than risk compromising his religious independence.
sufyan-al-thawri.scholarlyContribution: Formulated an early school of jurisprudence and collected core Kufan and Iraqi hadith transmissions.

abdullah-ibn-yusuf.name: Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Tunisi
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.fullName: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Kila'i al-Dimashqi thumma al-Tunisi
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.arabicFullName: أبو محمد عبد الله بن يوسف الكلاعي الدمشقي ثم التنيسي المصري
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.grade: Thiqah Mutqin (Foremost transmitter of Malik's Muwatta)
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Mutqin, one of the most reliable transmitters of Malik
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.dhahabiGrade: Imam al-Hafiz, preferred by Bukhari above all others for narrating from Malik
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.biography: An outstanding transmitter of Syrian origin who settled in Egypt. Imam al-Bukhari considered him the most accurate and dependable narrator of Imam Malik's Muwatta', frequently choosing his transmissions for opening chapters of books in the Sahih.
abdullah-ibn-yusuf.scholarlyContribution: Direct teacher of Imam al-Bukhari and master conduit of Malik's legal traditions into Egypt.

musaddad-ibn-musarhad.name: Musaddad ibn Musarhad
musaddad-ibn-musarhad.fullName: Abu al-Hasan Musaddad ibn Musarhad ibn Musarbal al-Asadi al-Basri
musaddad-ibn-musarhad.arabicFullName: أبو الحسن مسدد بن مسرهد بن مسربل الأسدي البصري
musaddad-ibn-musarhad.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Hafiz, celebrated author of the large Musnad
musaddad-ibn-musarhad.dhahabiGrade: Imam, master of Basra, resolute champion of the prophetic traditions
musaddad-ibn-musarhad.biography: A primary teacher of Imam al-Bukhari and author of Musnad Musaddad. He was hailed by Yahya ibn Ma'in and Ahmad ibn Hanbal as an unshakeable mountain of reliability ("Musaddad is truthful, reliable, and whatever he narrates is solid").
musaddad-ibn-musarhad.scholarlyContribution: Crucial teacher of Bukhari, transmitting Iraqi and Basran hadiths with immense precision.

qutaibah-ibn-said.name: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id
qutaibah-ibn-said.fullName: Abu Raja Qutaybah ibn Sa'id ibn Jamil al-Thaqafi al-Balkhi
qutaibah-ibn-said.arabicFullName: أبو رجاء قتيبة بن سعيد بن جميل الثقفي مولاهم البلخي البغلاني
qutaibah-ibn-said.grade: Thiqah Thabt (Renowned Global Traveler for Hadith)
qutaibah-ibn-said.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, universally narrated from by all six canonical compilers (Al-Kutub al-Sittah)
qutaibah-ibn-said.dhahabiGrade: Shaikh al-Islam, master of Khurasan, unassailable in integrity
qutaibah-ibn-said.biography: Traveled the entire Muslim world twice, hearing hadiths from Malik, Al-Layth, Hammad ibn Zayd, and Sufyan. Remarkably, all six masters of the Kutub al-Sittah (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, Ibn Majah) narrated directly from him in their books.
qutaibah-ibn-said.scholarlyContribution: A universal bridge connecting eastern Khurasan with the heartlands of Madinah, Makkah, and Iraq.

abu-salih-al-samman.name: Abu Salih al-Samman
abu-salih-al-samman.fullName: Dhakwan Abu Salih al-Samman al-Ghatafani al-Madani
abu-salih-al-samman.arabicFullName: ذكوان أبو صالح السمان الزيات الغطفاني مولاهم المدني
abu-salih-al-samman.grade: Thiqah Thabt (Premier Companion of Abu Hurairah)
abu-salih-al-samman.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, one of the most reliable and prolific students of Abu Hurairah
abu-salih-al-samman.dhahabiGrade: Imam, Hujjah, foremost narrator of traditions in Madinah
abu-salih-al-samman.biography: A venerable Successor of Madinah who traded in clarified butter (samn) and oil. He spent years in the company of Abu Hurairah, memorizing his narrations with unmatched fidelity. Imam al-A'mash and Suhayl ibn Abi Salih relied upon him heavily.
abu-salih-al-samman.scholarlyContribution: Primary conduit for hundreds of Abu Hurairah's prophetic narrations.

al-amash.name: Al-A'mash
al-amash.fullName: Abu Muhammad Sulayman ibn Mihran al-Asadi al-Kahili al-Kufi
al-amash.arabicFullName: أبو محمد سليمان بن مهران الأسدي الكاهلي مولاهم الكوفي
al-amash.grade: Thiqah Hafiz - Quranic Reader and Master of Kufan Hadith
al-amash.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Hafiz Arif bil-Qira'at, pillar of Kufan scholarship
al-amash.dhahabiGrade: Shaikh al-Islam, master of hadith memorizers and Quran reciters
al-amash.biography: Known as Al-A'mash due to his weak eyesight, he was endowed with extraordinary memory and sharp wit. He knew four thousand hadiths by heart with exact chains, and led the public recitation of the Qur'an in Kufa for over half a century.
al-amash.scholarlyContribution: Unsurpassed authority on Kufan chains and Qur'anic variants.

hisham-ibn-urwah.name: Hisham ibn 'Urwah
hisham-ibn-urwah.fullName: Abu al-Mundhir Hisham ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr al-Qurashi al-Asadi
hisham-ibn-urwah.arabicFullName: أبو المنذر هشام بن عروة بن الزبير بن العوام القرشي الأسدي المدني
hisham-ibn-urwah.grade: Thiqah Thabt Imam (Pillar of Urwah's Traditions)
hisham-ibn-urwah.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Faqih Imam, main inheritor of the house of Zubayr's legal knowledge
hisham-ibn-urwah.dhahabiGrade: Imam, Hujjah, Shaikh of Madinah and Baghdad
hisham-ibn-urwah.biography: Son of the great jurist Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. He inherited his father's vast collection of books containing the hadiths of their maternal aunt 'A'isha. Later in life, he traveled to Iraq where major scholars like Abu Hanifah, Malik, and Shu'bah received narrations from him.
hisham-ibn-urwah.scholarlyContribution: Essential narrator transmitting 'A'isha's household sunnah and legal verdicts to the wider Muslim world.

qatadah.name: Qatadah ibn Di'amah
qatadah.fullName: Abu al-Khattab Qatadah ibn Di'amah ibn Qatadah al-Sadusi al-Basri
qatadah.arabicFullName: أبو الخطاب قتادة بن دعامة بن قتادة السدوسي البصري
qatadah.grade: Thiqah Thabt - Blind Polymath of Basra
qatadah.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, miracle of memory in Quranic exegesis and hadith
qatadah.dhahabiGrade: The exemplar of photographic retention; master of Arabic genealogy and Quranic tafsir
qatadah.biography: Born blind, Qatadah was blessed with a photographic auditory memory. He would listen to a scholar dictate an entire manuscript once and recite it verbatim without error. Ahmad ibn Hanbal called him "the most learned person in Basra." He served as the primary bridge for the narrations of Anas ibn Malik in Iraq.
qatadah.scholarlyContribution: One of the foremost authorities in Quranic commentary (Tafsir), Arabic language, and hadith transmission.

al-hasan-al-basri.name: Al-Hasan al-Basri
al-hasan-al-basri.fullName: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan Yasar al-Basri
al-hasan-al-basri.arabicFullName: أبو سعيد الحسن بن أبي الحسن يسار البصري
al-hasan-al-basri.grade: Imam, Sayyid al-Zuhhad (Leader of Ascetics and Preachers)
al-hasan-al-basri.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Faqih, famed for his eloquence, depth of heart, and spiritual mastery
al-hasan-al-basri.dhahabiGrade: Shaikh al-Islam, incomparable spiritual beacon of the early community
al-hasan-al-basri.biography: Born in Madinah during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who prayed for him: "O Allah, grant him deep understanding in religion and make him beloved to people." Raised in proximity to the Mothers of the Believers, he moved to Basra and became the most revered preacher, jurist, and spiritual guide of his era.
al-hasan-al-basri.scholarlyContribution: Profound legacy in Islamic spiritual psychology, pulpit rhetoric, and ethical jurisprudence.

ali-ibn-al-madini.name: 'Ali ibn al-Madini
ali-ibn-al-madini.fullName: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Madini al-Basri
ali-ibn-al-madini.arabicFullName: أبو الحسن علي بن عبد الله بن جعفر بن نجيح السعدي مولاهم المديني البصري
ali-ibn-al-madini.grade: Amir al-Mu'minin fil-Hadith - Master of Hidden Hadith Defects ('Ilal)
ali-ibn-al-madini.ibnHajarGrade: Imam, foremost authority on hadith defects and narrator biographies
ali-ibn-al-madini.dhahabiGrade: The master of all masters of 'Ilal (hidden defects), peer of Ahmad ibn Hanbal
ali-ibn-al-madini.biography: Imam al-Bukhari's revered mentor. Al-Bukhari famously confessed: "I never belittled myself in front of anyone except 'Ali ibn al-Madini." Renowned for his supreme mastery of hidden defects in hadith chains and intricate relations between narrators. Together with Ahmad ibn Hanbal, he safeguarded the science of hadith in Iraq.
ali-ibn-al-madini.scholarlyContribution: Pioneered treatises on 'Ilal al-Hadith (hadith defects) and the names and biographies of narrators.
teachers: His father Abd Allah ibn Ja'far

muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.name: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.fullName: Abu Musa Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna ibn Ubayd al-Anazi al-Basri (Known as Al-Zaman)
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.arabicFullName: أبو موسى محمد بن المثنى بن عبيد العنزي البصري المعروف بالزمن
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.grade: Thiqah Thabt (Celebrated Teacher of Canonical Authors)
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt, teacher of all six major hadith compilers
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.dhahabiGrade: Imam al-Hafiz, master of Basra, universally loved for his reliability
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.biography: A prominent Basran traditionist known by the moniker "Al-Zaman." Along with Bundar (Muhammad ibn Bashshar), he taught all six compilers of the Kutub al-Sittah. Imam al-Bukhari narrated hundreds of hadiths directly from him.
muhammad-ibn-al-muthanna.scholarlyContribution: Prolific teacher of the 3rd century canonical hadith authors; preserved Basran traditions intact.

yahya-ibn-bukayr.name: Yahya ibn Bukayr
yahya-ibn-bukayr.fullName: Abu Abd Allah Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn Bukayr al-Makhzumi al-Misri
yahya-ibn-bukayr.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الله يحيى بن عبد الله بن بكير المخزومي مولاهم المصري
yahya-ibn-bukayr.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah, especially precise in narrating from Al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Malik
yahya-ibn-bukayr.dhahabiGrade: Imam al-Hafiz, venerable scholar of Egypt and teacher of Bukhari
yahya-ibn-bukayr.biography: A leading Egyptian muhaddith who served as a primary conduit for the knowledge of Al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Imam Malik. Imam al-Bukhari relied upon his manuscripts extensively, particularly when recording narrations detailing early prophetic history and the beginning of Revelation.
yahya-ibn-bukayr.scholarlyContribution: Direct teacher of Bukhari, preserving Egyptian and Hijazi manuscripts of early hadith.

abdullah-ibn-abbas.name: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas
abdullah-ibn-abbas.fullName: Abu al-Abbas Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib al-Qurashi al-Hashimi
abdullah-ibn-abbas.arabicFullName: أبو العباس عبد الله بن عباس بن عبد المطلب القرشي الهاشمي رضي الله عنهما
abdullah-ibn-abbas.grade: Hibr al-Ummah (The Scholar of the Nation) & Turjuman al-Qur'an
abdullah-ibn-abbas.ibnHajarGrade: The ocean of Quranic exegesis, for whom the Prophet ﷺ supplicated for wisdom
abdullah-ibn-abbas.dhahabiGrade: The Grand Master of Islamic exegesis, cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
abdullah-ibn-abbas.biography: The paternal cousin of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The Prophet embraced him in childhood and prayed: "O Allah, grant him deep comprehension in the religion and teach him interpretation of the Book." He became universally recognized by senior Companions as the preeminent authority in Quranic commentary (Tafsir), legal reasoning, and Arabic eloquence.
abdullah-ibn-abbas.scholarlyContribution: Narrated 1,660 hadiths; laid the foundational principles of systematic Quranic exegesis (Tafsir al-Qur'an).

abu-said-al-khudri.name: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri
abu-said-al-khudri.fullName: Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Sinan al-Ansari al-Khazraji al-Khudri
abu-said-al-khudri.arabicFullName: سعد بن مالك بن سنان الأنصاري الخزرجي الخدري رضي الله عنه
abu-said-al-khudri.grade: Sahabi 'Adl - One of the Prolific Seven Narrators
abu-said-al-khudri.ibnHajarGrade: Eminent Companion who participated in twelve expeditions with the Prophet ﷺ
abu-said-al-khudri.dhahabiGrade: Imam, Mufti of Madinah, prominent young companion of profound asceticism and piety
abu-said-al-khudri.biography: An illustrious Ansar Companion from Banu Khudra in Madinah. Presented by his father to fight at Uhud at age thirteen, he was judged too young, but subsequently accompanied the Prophet ﷺ in twelve major military campaigns. He was famed for his scrupulous piety, patient endurance during financial distress, and devotion to teaching hadiths in the Prophet's Mosque.
abu-said-al-khudri.scholarlyContribution: Narrated 1,170 hadiths, ranking among the top seven most prolific narrators of the Sunnah.

muadh-ibn-jabal.name: Mu'adh ibn Jabal
muadh-ibn-jabal.fullName: Abu Abd al-Rahman Mu'adh ibn Jabal ibn Amr al-Ansari al-Khazraji
muadh-ibn-jabal.arabicFullName: أبو عبد الرحمن معاذ بن جبل بن عمرو الأنصاري الخزرجي رضي الله عنه
muadh-ibn-jabal.grade: Sahabi 'Adl - Foremost in Knowledge of the Halal and Haram
muadh-ibn-jabal.ibnHajarGrade: The leader of the scholars on the Day of Resurrection, sent by the Prophet ﷺ as judge to Yemen
muadh-ibn-jabal.dhahabiGrade: Imam al-Kabir, peerless in jurisprudence and moral nobility
muadh-ibn-jabal.biography: Pledged allegiance at the Second Aqabah pledge as a youth. The Prophet ﷺ declared: "The most knowledgeable of my nation regarding the lawful and the unlawful is Mu'adh ibn Jabal." He was commissioned by the Prophet ﷺ as supreme judge, teacher, and administrator to Yemen, establishing the principles of judicial ijtihad.
muadh-ibn-jabal.scholarlyContribution: Pioneered legal reasoning (ijtihad) and structured provincial Islamic governance and education.

adam-ibn-abi-iyas.name: Adam ibn Abi Iyas
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.fullName: Abu al-Hasan Adam ibn Abi Iyas Nasr al-Asqalani
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.arabicFullName: أبو الحسن آدم بن أبي إياس نصر العسقلاني الخراساني الأصل
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.grade: Thiqah Thabt Zahid (Venerable Teacher of Bukhari)
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.ibnHajarGrade: Thiqah Thabt Abid, one of the premier scholars of the borderlands of the Levant
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.dhahabiGrade: Imam al-Hafiz, ascetic leader and teacher of Imam al-Bukhari
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.biography: A venerable scholar of Khurasani descent who settled in the frontier city of Asqalan in Palestine. Known for immense asceticism, Quranic contemplation, and weeping in prayers. Imam al-Bukhari heard thousands of hadiths from him, relying upon him for foundational traditions in belief and manners.
adam-ibn-abi-iyas.scholarlyContribution: Direct teacher of Imam al-Bukhari; major authority on the transmissions of Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj.
